subject: question mediation analyses with clustered data

messages.author: 103216590b55b6a4
messages.subject: question mediation analyses with clustered data
parts:
Dear all,

I have conducted a study that aims to evaluate the effectiveness of a teacher training against bullying of school.
To this end 10 schools were randomly assigned to an intervention or control condition (5schools in each condition) and variables of interest were assessed using questionnaires at a pre- and post-test assessment (thus two waves). 

The main aims of the study are to test
  1. intervention effects on teachers' responses to bullying (continuous variable)
  2. intervention effects on level of bullying victimization (continuous variable)
  3. test whether the effects of the intervention on victimization are mediated by the teachers' responses to bullying (intervention --> teacher responses --> bullying victimization)
We have three levels of data (namely: waves (level 1) nested in students (level 2) nested in classrooms (level 3)). The intervention variable is a level 3 variable; and the other variables (teachers' responses and bullying victimization) are level 1 variables (measured using student report at both waves).

At this point I don't have any experience yet with mediation analyses with clustered/longitudinal data. My question is whether Lavaan would allow to test our model (and if so, if you can recommend any examples of similar previous analyses) or whether multilevel analyses (instead of SEM) are more recommended here?

Thanks in advance!
Chloë

messages.author: f1530326ce101401
messages.subject: Re: question mediation analyses with clustered data
parts:
Hi Chloë

As far as I know, this cannot be done in lavaan (yet). The following is stated in the lavaan tutorial: "If the data is clustered, one way to handle the clustering is to use a multilevel modeling approach. In the SEM framework, this leads to multilevel SEM. The multilevel capabilities of lavaan are still limited, but you can fit a two-level SEM with random intercepts (note: only when all data is continuous).".  Furthermore, I cannot find anything regarding three-level SEM in the tutorial or version control.

Perhaps this can be done with MPlus, but I am not sure.  Maybe someone with more experience can provide better feedback or guidance regarding an alternative.

Best wishes,

Jasper

messages.author: b8fd92e5e3662745
messages.subject: Re: question mediation analyses with clustered data
parts:
Chloe, you have 8 degrees of freedom (10 clusters minus two means per condition) for your analysis. You just can't squeeze much modeling into this if you are attempting inference with respect to randomization / cluster assignment.

If you want to consider treatment as "just a variable" then of course you can build whatever models you want. Multilevel SEMs can be fit in Stata with -sem- / -gsem- commands.
